<thought>Based on the available data (C12H16O5Cl, 5 DBE, 11 aromatic carbons, one CH₃, one carbonyl, and the 13C NMR shifts indicating an aromatic ring, a carbonyl, an O‑CH₂ group and a methyl), a reasonable way to split the molecule is into an aromatic fragment that contains the chlorine and the carbonyl functionality, and a small aliphatic fragment that provides the ethoxy side‑chain. These two fragments can be joined through an ester linkage to give the full structure.</thought>
<final_answer>['Clc1ccc(C(=O)O)cc1', 'CCO']</final_answer>
